summary: This component renders a button that copies a blog post's plain Markdown version to the clipboard and a link to view the raw file. When you click the button, it fetches the `.md` file that mirrors the current HTML post, copies its text to your clipboard, and shows feedback messages like 'Copied' or 'Could not copy'. After two seconds, it resets back to the default button text.

explanations.10: This type restricts the status variable to only one of these four specific string values, preventing invalid states like 'loading' or 'pending'.
explanations.27: This constructs the URL to the Markdown file by taking the current page's permalink and appending `.md` instead of trailing slashes—so `/blog/my-post/` becomes `/blog/my-post.md`.
explanations.29: useCallback wraps the copy function so it stays the same reference between renders, which prevents unnecessary re-runs of the useEffect below.
explanations.32: fetch() downloads the Markdown file from the server.
explanations.33: res.ok is false if the HTTP status is in the 400+ range; throwing an error here triggers the catch block so the component shows 'Could not copy'.
explanations.35: navigator.clipboard.writeText() puts the text into your browser's clipboard so you can paste it elsewhere.
explanations.44: This early return skips setting the timer if the status is still 'idle' or 'copying', so the button only auto-resets after showing success or error feedback.
explanations.45: setTimeout with a 2000ms delay schedules the status to reset back to 'idle', making the feedback message disappear after two seconds.
explanations.46: Returning a cleanup function from useEffect cancels the timeout if the component unmounts or status changes again before the timer fires.
